title: Alex's Rules
subtitle: Read before the bell. The market pays for discipline, not for being right.

rules.rule: Entry, stop and target — say all three out loud before you click.
rules.why: If you cannot state all three, you do not have a trade. You have an opinion.

rules.rule: Trade the plan you wrote before the open, not the one you invent at 10:05.
rules.why: The plan was written by the calm version of you. The 10:05 version has money on the line.

rules.rule: Size from the stop distance, never from how confident you feel.
rules.why: Confidence is not information. The stop is the only thing that decides what a loss costs.

rules.rule: Set the maximum you will lose today before the open. When you hit it, you are done.
rules.why: The number is easy to pick at 8am and impossible to pick at 2pm down three trades.

rules.rule: No setup, no trade. Boredom is not a signal.
rules.why: Most days have two or three real setups. Everything else is the market taking commissions.

rules.rule: If you missed the entry, you missed the trade.
rules.why: The setup had a price. Above that price it is a different trade with worse odds and a wider stop.

rules.rule: A stock that already ran to your target is not an entry. It is someone else's exit.
rules.why: You would be buying the profit of whoever got in at the level you were watching.

rules.rule: If price is more than one ATR past your level, the trade is gone. Wait for the pullback or move on.
rules.why: Entering extended means your stop is now further away and your target is now closer. Both sides get worse.

rules.rule: The next setup is not a reward for missing this one, and not a punishment either.
rules.why: Treating the next trade as a make-up trade is how one miss becomes three losses.

rules.rule: Urgency is the signal to stand up, not to click.
rules.why: Nothing about a good setup requires you to hurry. The feeling of hurry is information about you, not the chart.

rules.rule: Watch the level, not the P&L in dollars.
rules.why: Dollars make you exit winners early and hold losers long. The level tells you whether you are still right.

rules.rule: Never add to a loser to improve the average.
rules.why: You are increasing risk precisely when the trade is telling you the read was wrong.

rules.rule: Revenge trading is the most expensive habit in the market.
rules.why: The market does not know you lost, and will not give it back because you asked louder.

rules.rule: Protect a green day. After a good gain, cut size or stop.
rules.why: Giving back a winning day costs twice: the money, and the belief that you can hold a win.

rules.rule: Greed is just an exit you did not plan.
rules.why: If the target was written down, taking it is not leaving money behind. It is doing the job.

rules.rule: Take the stop. Every time.
rules.why: The stop is the cost of being wrong, and being wrong is a normal, budgeted part of the work.

rules.rule: Never move a stop away from price. Closer is fine, further is never fine.
rules.why: Widening a stop converts a planned small loss into an unplanned large one.

rules.rule: If the reason you entered is gone, exit — even at breakeven, even at a small profit.
rules.why: You are not paid for holding. You are paid for being in position while the reason holds.

rules.rule: Two losses in a row: stand up and walk away for ten minutes.
rules.why: The third trade after two losses is almost never taken by the calm version of you.

rules.rule: Grade the execution, not the outcome.
rules.why: A well-executed trade can lose and a reckless one can win. Only one of those is repeatable.

rules.rule: Log every trade, including the good setups you correctly skipped.
rules.why: The skips are evidence of discipline, and they are invisible unless you write them down.

rules.rule: One setup executed a hundred times beats ten setups executed once.
rules.why: An edge is a thing you can measure. You cannot measure something you only did once.

rules.rule: Write one line: what did I do today that I would not want to repeat?
rules.why: The leak is usually the same leak. Naming it is most of the fix.
